records.text: White now has a passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or the adjacent files. A status defined by what is absent; I like that.
Black now has a passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or the adjacent files. A status defined by what is absent; I like that.
The better move would have given White a passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or its neighbors, though other pieces would still matter.
The better move would have given Black a passed pawn. No enemy pawn ahead on its file or its neighbors, though other pieces would still matter.
White now has an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn on an adjacent file; isolation here is a matter of neighbors.
Black now has an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn on an adjacent file; isolation here is a matter of neighbors.
The better move would have left White an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn on the neighboring files, regardless of what the pieces might defend.
The better move would have left Black an isolated pawn. No friendly pawn on the neighboring files, regardless of what the pieces might defend.
White's pawns now share a file: doubled pawns. An arrangement to examine, not a verdict by itself.
Black's pawns now share a file: doubled pawns. An arrangement to examine, not a verdict by itself.
With the better move, White would have doubled pawns. The pawns would share a file; the better choice can still have that shape.
With the better move, Black would have doubled pawns. The pawns would share a file; the better choice can still have that shape.
White's rook occupies an open file now. No pawns of either color along it. Open describes the pawns, not everything the rook might meet.
Black's rook occupies an open file now. No pawns of either color along it. Open describes the pawns, not everything the rook might meet.
Open counts only the pawns here. With the better move, White's rook would have occupied a file with none, though pieces could still be there.
Open counts only the pawns here. With the better move, Black's rook would have occupied a file with none, though pieces could still be there.
The file is half-open from White's rook's perspective: its own pawns are absent, while enemy pawns remain. The name depends on which side is looking.
The file is half-open from Black's rook's perspective: its own pawns are absent, while enemy pawns remain. The name depends on which side is looking.
Half-open would describe the file from White's rook's side after the better move. No friendly pawns there, but enemy pawns would remain.
Half-open would describe the file from Black's rook's side after the better move. No friendly pawns there, but enemy pawns would remain.
White's knight has gained a defender where it had none. Interesting how a piece's situation changes through a connection.
Black's knight has gained a defender where it had none. Interesting how a piece's situation changes through a connection.
What changed for White's bishop is a relationship: it now has a defender where it had none.
What changed for Black's bishop is a relationship: it now has a defender where it had none.
White's rook has acquired something it cannot provide for itself: a defender. It had none before.
Black's rook has acquired something it cannot provide for itself: a defender. It had none before.
White's queen has acquired a defender. Even a queen's support can go from absent to present.
Black's queen has acquired a defender. Even a queen's support can go from absent to present.
The better move would change who supports White's knight: from no defender to having one.
The better move would change who supports Black's knight: from no defender to having one.
White's bishop would have gained its missing defense with the better move. Compare the support, not just the piece.
Black's bishop would have gained its missing defense with the better move. Compare the support, not just the piece.
White's rook had no defender. With the better move, another piece would take on that relationship and defend it.
Black's rook had no defender. With the better move, another piece would take on that relationship and defend it.
For White's queen, the better move would change a relationship: a defender would cover it where none had before.
For Black's queen, the better move would change a relationship: a defender would cover it where none had before.
White's knight has lost all its defenders. That describes its support, not whether it can be captured.
Black's knight has lost all its defenders. That describes its support, not whether it can be captured.
White's bishop was defended before this move; now it is not. The missing connection is the relevant observation.
Black's bishop was defended before this move; now it is not. The missing connection is the relevant observation.
White's rook has become undefended. Its support has vanished, though that alone does not establish a loss.
Black's rook has become undefended. Its support has vanished, though that alone does not establish a loss.
White's queen no longer has a defender. A powerful piece can still have no support; those are different properties.
Black's queen no longer has a defender. A powerful piece can still have no support; those are different properties.
The better move would have left White's knight without its defenders. A better position can contain an undefended piece.
The better move would have left Black's knight without its defenders. A better position can contain an undefended piece.
White's bishop would have lost its remaining defense with the better move. Undefended would describe it; lost would require more evidence.
Black's bishop would have lost its remaining defense with the better move. Undefended would describe it; lost would require more evidence.
The better choice would have removed all defense of White's rook. That is a support change, not proof of a capture.
The better choice would have removed all defense of Black's rook. That is a support change, not proof of a capture.
With the better move, White's queen would have lost the defense it had. The stronger option still deserves that inspection.
With the better move, Black's queen would have lost the defense it had. The stronger option still deserves that inspection.
The knight makes its first departure from its starting square. Development is a beginning, quite literally.
A knight has moved for the first time. I can mark that piece's development now.
The knight's original square is behind it for the first time. That is the development to notice.
First movement for this knight: it leaves its starting square. A piece begins its journey through the position.
A bishop leaves its starting square for the first time. An arrival into play, seen from the bishop's perspective.
The bishop has begun moving. Its first departure from home is development.
That bishop has now made its first move from the original square. A small event with a name: development.
The bishop was still on its starting square; now it has made its first departure. A visible beginning.
The better option would have given a knight its first move from home. I would follow that beginning on the board.
A knight would have left its original square for the first time with the better choice. Development is part of that option.
The better move would have started that knight's development. Its first departure was possible.
Consider the knight's starting square: with the better move, it would have left that square for the first time.
A bishop's first departure was part of the better option. That move would have developed it.
The better choice would have brought a bishop off its starting square for the first time. A different beginning for the position.
That bishop could have started moving with the better move. Its development would have begun there.
With the better option, a bishop would have made its first move from home. I would watch how play follows that beginning.
The stronger possibility was not chosen. The position gives up value compared with that option.
Comparing the choices reveals the cost: this move is weaker than the best available alternative.
This selection leaves a worse position than the stronger move would have. The comparison matters more than the appearance.
One position, two choices, different results. This move leaves less value than the stronger alternative.
The other side has an immediate capture. Availability first; the value of the exchange is another question.
A capture is possible right away for the opponent. I would inspect what follows before calling it a gain.
The reply can take something immediately. A concrete option for the other side, whatever it turns out to cost.
Notice the opponent's capture option. It can happen on the very next move.
You used the chance from their last error. I like seeing the mistake and the response connected that clearly.
Their previous mistake became your opportunity, and you took it. That connection is worth remembering.
The opponent's error did not go unused. Your response made something of it.
The better choice offers a useful comparison with the move played.
There is a stronger alternative worth putting beside this choice.
Compare the replies after the stronger option; that is where I would look next.
The pawn was passed already; now it has advanced toward promotion. Its status is the same, its distance is not.
That passed pawn is nearer promotion now. I would follow the reply before looking any further along its route.
The strongest response gives check. That makes the king's immediate safety the next question to resolve.
A check is the best reply here. Whatever else is happening, that check demands an answer.
That matches the lesson's intended move. The example and your choice agree.
Correct for this lesson. I can see the taught move in your answer.
You supplied the move the lesson calls for. A precise match.
That step is correct. The puzzle still has another part to investigate.
A match with the solution so far. Keep looking; the puzzle continues.
You found the right move here. The next part of the puzzle remains to be solved.
Your move matches the opening line being practiced. Recall made visible.
That's the move stored in your repertoire. The remembered line and the board agree.
The opening answer matches your study. An exact connection between practice and the chosen move.
A best move. I find that kind of precision satisfying.
Best is the verdict here. A choice worth examining closely.
A sound choice, though a stronger move exists. I can appreciate the distinction.
Good, without being best. A useful reminder that sound choices need not be perfect.
